Many of you experienced with the Fedora operating system are no doubt familiar with the (now former) package tool YUM. As of Fedora 22 YUM has been depreciated in favor of Fedora's new packaging tool DNF. To help everyone out here are some articles explaining the reasoning behind the switch, differences between YUM and DNF, as well as commands to help you transition over and make better use of DNF itself:

  • DNF - Wikipedia
  • DNF – The Next Generation Package Management Utility for RPM Based Distributions - Tecmint
  • 27 ‘DNF’ (Fork of Yum) Commands for RPM Package Management in Linux - Tecmint
  • DNF Is The New Default Package Manager Of Fedora 22 - UNIXMen
  • Changes in DNF CLI compared to Yum - ReadTheDocs.org
  • Package Management - Fedora Administrator's Guide
YUM is dead... All hail DNF!
What happens to Yum extender? Does it become DNF extender?

In Fedora 22 Yum itself is still included, but it's depreciated and if you try and run it it will still work, but it will tell you that you probably should be using DNF instead. As such the older traditional YumEx is still available, but Fedora 22 also ships with a new version of YumEx called "Yum Extender DNF" which is powered by DNF. I'm not sure if they plan on renaming it in the future, but for now both the "old" and the "new" Yum Extenders are available.
FYI, the Fedora System Administrator's Guide for F22 has a full chapter on DNF with a bunch of useful info.
